summary: Hybrid cloud + on-premises integration: React (Vite SPA) (web) on .NET 10 LTS + ASP.NET Core with Azure SQL Database (serverless/General Purpose) — Central India (Pune), hosted on Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B1 and up) — Central India (Pune). Estimated $51-276/month.

frontend.justification: Web: React (Vite SPA) — Rich interactive app screens; team already writes javascript for the UI; internal app behind login needs no SEO; good fast delivery (you weighted it 5/5); good low running cost (you weighted it 3/5).

alternatives.why_not: React (Vite SPA) is stronger on: good fast delivery (you weighted it 5/5) (priorities.time_to_market); rich interactive app screens (project.type). Overall 2.2 points behind.
Learning curve 3/5 for an intermediate team (team.experience). React (Vite SPA) is stronger on: good low running cost (you weighted it 3/5) (priorities.cost). Overall 4.8 points behind.

tradeoffs: Client-rendered pages are weak for SEO

backend.justification: Team already writes csharp for the API; first-class SQL Server driver/ORM; mature security/audit tooling; good maintainability (you weighted it 5/5); good security (you weighted it 4/5).

alternatives.why_not: .NET 10 LTS + ASP.NET Core is stronger on: first-class SQL Server driver/ORM (infrastructure.existing_systems); good security (you weighted it 4/5) (priorities.security). Overall 9.6 points behind.

.NET 10 LTS + ASP.NET Core is stronger on: good maintainability (you weighted it 5/5) (priorities.maintainability); good security (you weighted it 4/5) (priorities.security). Overall 17.4 points behind.

tradeoffs: Smaller open-source hosting choice outside Azure

database.choice: Azure SQL Database (serverless/General Purpose) — Central India (Pune)
database.justification: Matches the existing On-prem SQL Server 2019 the team already runs; EF Core + SQL Server is the default .NET pairing; team knows SQL; good maintainability (you weighted it 5/5); good security (you weighted it 4/5). New application data lives in the cloud database; the on-prem server is integrated, not migrated (see supporting 'other').

alternatives.choice: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17
alternatives.why_not: Azure SQL Database (serverless/General Purpose) is stronger on: matches the existing On-prem SQL Server 2019 the team already runs (infrastructure.existing_systems); EF Core + SQL Server is the default .NET pairing (team.languages). Overall 6.7 points behind.

alternatives.choice: Azure Database for MySQL – Flexible Server 8.4
alternatives.why_not: Azure SQL Database (serverless/General Purpose) is stronger on: matches the existing On-prem SQL Server 2019 the team already runs (infrastructure.existing_systems); good maintainability (you weighted it 5/5) (priorities.maintainability). Overall 13.9 points behind.
Excluded: a separate vendor outside the explicit cloud_preference azure (infrastructure.cloud_preference).

tradeoffs: Licence cost outside Azure SQL; Windows-centric tooling

hosting.choice: Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B1 and up) — Central India (Pune)
hosting.justification: Satisfies the hard constraints (cloud_preference azure, managed_cloud (no servers to patch), data_residency india -> Central India (Pune)). Hybrid Connections reach the existing on-prem database without opening inbound ports; built-in Entra ID sign-in (Easy Auth); quick to set up for a 6-week MVP; good maintainability (you weighted it 5/5); good fast delivery (you weighted it 5/5).

alternatives.why_not: Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B1 and up) is stronger on: good maintainability (you weighted it 5/5) (priorities.maintainability); good fast delivery (you weighted it 5/5) (priorities.time_to_market). Overall 13.8 points behind.
Excluded: runs on cloudflare, but cloud_preference is azure (infrastructure.cloud_preference).
Excluded: runs on aws, but cloud_preference is azure (infrastructure.cloud_preference).

tradeoffs: Hybrid Connections limited to 5 per Basic plan
Less control than containers for unusual runtimes

supporting.choice: Microsoft Entra ID (existing tenant) via OpenID Connect
supporting.justification: enterprise_sso is required and 'Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD)' already exists: reuse it so employees keep one login; app roles/groups in the token drive approvals and admin rights.

alternatives.why_not: duplicates an identity provider the company already operates
extra hop and a second directory to administer

tradeoffs: Depends on the customer's Entra tenant admins for app registration and consent

supporting.justification: Uploads (images, documents) go straight from clients to object storage via signed URLs. Private bucket, server-generated signed URLs, encryption with managed keys.

alternatives.why_not: bloats backups and costs more per GB
zero egress fees, but a second vendor outside AZURE

supporting.justification: Automated tests and deploys on every push to Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B1 and up); free minutes cover a team of 2.

alternatives.why_not: equivalent; GitHub chosen for its marketplace of deploy actions

tradeoffs: Secrets must be stored as encrypted environment secrets

supporting.choice: Azure Monitor + Application Insights in Central India (Pune)
supporting.justification: Logs and metrics stay with the host provider in Central India (Pune); alerts on error rate and latency against the 800 ms p95 target.

alternatives.why_not: stores data only in the US or EU

tradeoffs: Log retention costs grow with traffic

supporting.choice: Microsoft Graph notifications (Outlook mail / Teams) for approvals
supporting.justification: Approval requests and decisions reach managers in the Microsoft 365 tools they already use, authorised through the existing Entra tenant.

alternatives.why_not: duplicates mail infrastructure the company already has

tradeoffs: Needs admin consent for Graph application permissions

supporting.choice: Integration with existing On-prem SQL Server 2019 via App Service Hybrid Connection (outbound 443 relay, no inbound ports)
supporting.justification: Reuse the existing SQL Server data in place: read reference data through a narrow repository layer over a private network path; add new app tables only with the DBA's agreement. The new application keeps its own tables in Azure SQL Database (serverless/General Purpose) and reads the existing data through App Service Hybrid Connection (outbound 443 relay, no inbound ports).

alternatives.choice: Migrate everything into the new database now
alternatives.why_not: risky in the MVP timeline and breaks existing consumers

alternatives.choice: Use the on-prem server as the only database
alternatives.why_not: ties availability of the new app to the on-prem server and the relay

tradeoffs: Cross-network latency on queries to the on-prem server
Credentials for the on-prem database must live in a secret store

assumptions: Hosting Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B1 and up): $30-150/month at the 'small' tier.
observability: Azure Monitor + Application Insights in Central India (Pune) $5-30/month.
Stored data ~20 GB after 12 months at ~$0.02-0.035/GB-month (year-end volume used as an upper bound, not an average).
Excluded: taxes, domain names, paid support plans and data-egress spikes. Order-of-magnitude band, not a quote.

warnings.message: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certifies your organisation's ISMS, not a cloud provider's badge: keep asset inventory, access reviews, logging and change management for this system.
'On-prem SQL Server 2019' is in extended (security-only) support until 2030-01-09; supported, but plan the upgrade path.

assumptions: Knowledge base as of 2026-11-10; lifecycle and pricing judgements use that date, not the run date.
Scale tier 'small' from 1,500 users and ~300 peak concurrent users (people, not requests per second; used only for sizing and cost).
